correctness.rationale: The LD-set characterization is reconstructed directly: a set meeting both bipartition classes is LD exactly when it omits at most one vertex from each class, while a one-side set can be LD only when it is the whole side opposite a singleton class. This gives a three-block construction for every biclique of order at least three, an upper bound of three for stars, an upper bound of four when both sides have size at least two, and a contradiction to four blocks unless both sides have size two. The exceptional four-singleton partition of K_{2,2} and the K_{1,1} obstruction are checked explicitly. Exhaustive finite replay matches the theorem on all tested cases.

value.rationale: Complete bipartite graphs are a canonical infinite family, and the invariant was introduced in 2026 with exact-family determination as a central theme. The result gives a complete infinite classification, including existence, a unique exceptional jump at K_{2,2}, and a structural explanation via LD-set complements. It is not a numerical recomputation or arbitrary slice; it resolves the new coalition parameter on one of the standard graph families against which domination-type invariants are routinely tested.
